jobs.title: Senior Director, Finance Transformation-EN
jobs.description:
Behind every success is a team of dedicated experts driving us forward. Our corporate functions don’t just support — they lead, shaping the company’s path and preparing clients and employees for the moments that matter. Be part of a team where your work makes a difference, with opportunities to grow, collaborate, and thrive.

The Senior Director, Finance Transformation
will play a key role in advancing CAE's finance transformation vision by translating enterprise priorities into a structured portfolio of measurable, technology-enabled improvements across the global Finance function.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), this individual will serve as a strategic leader responsible for defining and driving the global Finance and enterprise transformation agenda. The role is focused on leading large-scale initiatives related to process optimization, margin improvement, cost efficiency, and digital transformation.

The incumbent will oversee the global Finance transformation roadmap and project portfolio, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives and delivering measurable outcomes in financial performance, efficiency, scalability, growth enablement, and innovation. As a transformation leader, this individual will foster cross-functional collaboration, lead change management and communication efforts, and support executive decision-making through high-impact initiatives and reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Define the global Finance transformation strategy and translate enterprise objectives and long-term business priorities into a clear and structured roadmap.
Own and govern the Finance Transformation portfolio, including prioritization, investment planning, and delivery of high-impact initiatives.
Establish and lead robust governance frameworks to ensure cross-functional alignment, accountability, and effective decision-making across global initiatives.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of large-scale transformation programs, including scope definition, resource allocation, risk management, and value realization.
Champion operational excellence and process standardization across the global Finance function by leveraging continuous improvement methodologies.
Lead the evaluation, selection, and deployment of strategic technologies, including automation, artificial intelligence, and advanced analytics, to improve the efficiency, control, and scalability of Finance operations.
Develop and execute the Finance transformation change management strategy, ensuring stakeholder engagement, adoption, and alignment across teams.
Partner with senior leaders across Finance, IT, and Business Units to identify, prioritize, and execute transformation opportunities while accelerating innovation.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), value-tracking mechanisms, and reporting processes to measure transformation impact and support executive decision-making.
Build organizational capability by coaching and developing Finance teams while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Lead post-implementation reviews to validate benefit realization, capture lessons learned, and strengthen governance and process ownership.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or postgraduate degree in Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience, including senior leadership roles within Finance.
Proven experience leading finance transformation programs within complex global organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong experience in project management and continuous improvement; Six Sigma certification is considered an asset.
Strategic mindset with the ability to translate organizational priorities into actionable plans, governance frameworks, and measurable outcomes.
Deep expertise in digital finance technologies, automation, artificial intelligence, and analytics platforms, with the ability to assess and implement practical solutions that enhance Finance effectiveness and scalability.
Significant experience in governance, stakeholder management, and executive-level influence.
Demonstrated ability to build relationships, drive results, inspire creativity, and foster innovation across functions and geographies.
Ability to lead through ambiguity, influence without direct authority, and align diverse stakeholder groups around common objectives.
High level of resilience and ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level presentation capabilities.

Benefits

Comprehensive group insurance program.
Telemedicine program and Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
Employee Share Purchase Plan.
Group Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
CAE Defined Benefit Pension Plan.
Sabbatical leave program.
Flexible work arrangements.
Enhanced parental leave benefits.

About CAE

At CAE, our mission is clear: to help make the world a safer place. For nearly 80 years, we’ve driven innovation in simulation, training, and mission readiness to support critical operations worldwide. By leveraging advanced technologies, we empower our customers to operate smarter, faster, and more sustainably. Join a purpose-driven organization where bold ideas are encouraged, collaboration drives progress, and your growth fuels our shared success.

Regular

Join us and be part of a team that's committed to making a real difference and be part of something meaningful.

What’s in it for you

Benefits

We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a permanent employee:

About The Role

Join the Audit and Evaluation team, in the Director, Strategy and Audit Operations position. This role plays a pivotal leadership role and is responsible for shaping and delivering internal audit strategies, plans, and services that strengthen corporate governance, risk management, and internal controls.

The Director provides strategic insight to help the organization anticipate emerging risks and evolving priorities, ensuring the internal audit function remains forward-looking and value-driven. By identifying trends and translating insights into action, this role supports the achievement of CMHC’s corporate objectives and key strategic priorities.

What You’ll Do

Provide strategic leadership for internal audit activities, ensuring audit plans, methodologies, and engagements align with IIA standards, regulatory expectations, and organizational priorities.
Serve as a trusted enterprise advisor, identifying forward-looking risks, opportunities, and efficiencies that enhance corporate performance and support CMHC’s risk appetite.
Shape and deliver risk based audit strategies and multiyear plans, monitoring performance against audit objectives and key indicators.
Oversee the approval and communication of internal audit reports, risk assessments, and related products to senior management, Executive Committees, and the Audit Committee.
Strengthen corporate governance by providing assurance and insight on governance frameworks, risk management practices, and internal controls.
Lead innovation within the audit function, including the use of data analytics, artificial intelligence, and agile audit techniques to drive efficiency and insight.
Influence decision making at the executive and Board level by clearly presenting complex findings and actionable recommendations.
Build and maintain strong internal and external partnerships, including with second line functions, OSFI, and external auditors.
Oversee enterprise level risk identification and analysis, anticipating emerging risks and recommending improvements to mitigate exposure.
Lead and develop a high performing, inclusive team, promoting accountability, continuous learning, stewardship of resources, and a respectful, diverse workplace.

What You Should Have

An undergraduate degree in accounting, management, finance, risk management, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
A minimum of 13 years of experience in public accounting and/or internal audit, including at least 5 years in a supervisory or leadership role.
A proven track record of leading a professional internal audit function, with deep expertise in internal auditing and accounting principles and practices.
Authoritative knowledge of Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) standards, leading practices, internal audit methodologies, and financial institution control environments.
Strong understanding of complex organizational mandates, business objectives, programs, and regulatory frameworks within a large, regulated environment.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey complex issues and influence senior leaders and Board level audiences in both French and English.
Advanced analytical and problem solving skills, with the ability to synthesize information into clear, actionable insights for executive decision making.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results under tight timelines.
Sound judgment, tact, and discretion when dealing with sensitive, confidential, or high impact matters.

jobs.title: Leader Amélioration de la Donnée / Data Improvement Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

Leader Amélioration des Données / Data Improvement Lead

English job description follows***

Description De L'emploi

Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans l'analyse de données et la gestion de la performance, vous avez travaillé sur l'amélioration de processus et la digitalisation, et vous souhaitez évoluer tout en développant de nouvelles compétences ? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Leader en amélioration des données pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance Management basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous collaborez étroitement avec les analystes de performance, les équipes des Opérations et l'équipe de digitalisation.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Performance Management chargée de développer la standardisation et l'amélioration de la qualité des données de performance pour la chaîne de valeur A220, tout en soutenant la feuille de route de digitalisation. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale et l'autonomie, dans un esprit de soutien mutuel et d'apprentissage collectif.

Dans ce rôle, vous agirez en tant que point de contact central et facilitateur entre les analystes de la performance opérationnelle et l'équipe de digitalisation. Votre mission sera d'optimiser l'efficacité des processus d'assemblage de l'A220 en coordonnant l'amélioration des données provenant de divers flux : approvisionnement secondaire, SDO ( Supplier Disruption Over Cost ), coûts récurrents (RC) et CVAT ( Customer Value Added Time ). Vous identifierez les besoins en automatisation, harmoniserez les méthodes d'analyse et assurerez la transition des analyses manuelles vers des solutions digitales robustes pour améliorer la rentabilité globale.

Votre Environnement De Travail

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce Que Nous Prenons Soin De Vous

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride (selon les besoins opérationnels), une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais, service médical sur site, accès à un service de navette publique entre Laval (station de métro Montmorency) et Mirabel, et une application de covoiturage.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos Défis

Assurer le lien principal entre les analystes (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) et l'équipe de digitalisation pour traduire les besoins métiers en solutions automatisées;
Garantir la qualité, la cohérence et l'exactitude des données de performance issues des flux d'approvisionnement et de production;
Harmoniser la définition et le suivi des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) à travers les différents flux pour assurer une vision transverse de la performance;
Identifier les opportunités d'automatisation des rapports de performance (hebdomadaires, mensuels, trimestriels) et superviser leur mise en œuvre par l'équipe technique;
Consolider les points de blocage majeurs identifiés par les analystes du pôle Performance Management afin de prioriser la feuille de route de digitalisation selon l'impact sur la performance des opérations;
Préparer et présenter des feuilles de route claires et des visualisations de données aux parties prenantes pour soutenir la planification stratégique;
Collaborer avec les départements Opérations, Finances et Qualité pour optimiser la performance globale de la chaîne de valeur.

Votre Profil

Vous détenez un baccalauréat en ingénierie;
Vous détenez un minimum de 10 ans d’expérience dans un système industriel;
Vous possédez une expérience pertinente en analyse de données, en gestion de la performance ou en amélioration de processus;
Vous maîtrisez les outils d'analyse et de visualisation de données tels que Power BI, Skywise et Python;
Vous avez une connaissance approfondie des entrepôts de données, de l'analytique en nuage et de l'automatisation des processus;
Vous possédez de solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et une capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des équipes interfonctionnelles;
Vous avez la capacité de vulgariser des concepts de données complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux équipes opérationnelles et de direction;
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la définition de cadres de mesure de performance et la création de structures d'analyse complexes.

Ce poste peut impliquer des déplacements professionnels.

Déplacements Requis

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

Job Description

You have proven experience in data analysis and performance management? Have you worked on process improvement and digitalization, and are you looking to grow and develop new skills? This role is for you!

The A220 Commercial Aircraft Program is seeking a Data Improvement Leader to join our Performance Management team based in Mirabel (Quebec, Canada), where you will collaborate closely with performance analysts, Operations teams, and the digitalization team.

You will be part of the Performance Management team responsible for developing standardization and improving performance data quality for the A220 value chain, supporting the digitalization roadmap. The team is structured to promote cross-functional collaboration and autonomy, fostering mutual support and collective learning.

In this role, you will act as a central point of contact and facilitator between operational performance analysts and the digitalization team. Your mission will be to optimize the efficiency of the A220 assembly processes by coordinating data improvement across various streams: secondary supply, SDO (Supplier Disruption Over Cost), Recurring Costs (RC), and CVAT (Customer Value Added Time). You will identify automation needs, harmonize analytical methods, and ensure the transition from manual analysis to robust digital solutions to improve overall profitability.

Your Working Environment

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is headquartered in Mirabel, in the greater Montreal area, where the vibrant city of Montreal is just a stone’s throw away. Known for its peaceful and safe environment, the region offers a high quality of life for younger or experienced professionals and families, perfectly balancing career opportunities and outdoor activities that makes it a truly special place to call home.

How We Care For You

Financial rewards: Attractive salary, annual bonus, group insurance plan, pension plan and share purchase plan.
Work / Life Balance: A hybrid working policy (based on operational needs), on-site cafeterias and a highly competitive holiday policy.
Wellbeing/Health: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Discount Program, on-site Medical Service, access to a public shuttle service between Laval (Montmorency metro station) and Mirabel, and a carpooling application.
Individual development: Great upskilling opportunities and development prospects with unlimited access to +10.000 e-learning courses to develop your employability, certifications, accelerated development programmes, national and international mobility.

Your Challenges

Act as the primary liaison between analysts (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) and the digitalization team to translate business needs into automated solutions;
Ensure the quality, consistency, and accuracy of performance data collected from supply and production flows;
Harmonize the definition and monitoring of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across various flows to guarantee a cross-functional view of performance;
Identify automation opportunities for performance reporting (weekly, monthly, quarterly) and oversee their implementation by the technical team;
Consolidate major roadblocks identified by the Performance Management analysts to prioritize the digitalization roadmap based on its impact on Operational Performance;
Strategic Communication: Prepare and present clear roadmaps and data visualizations to stakeholders to support strategic planning;
Collaborate with Operations, Finance, and Quality teams to optimize the overall value chain performance.

Your Boarding Pass

You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering;
You have a minimum of 10 years of experience in an industrial system;
You possess relevant experience in data analysis, performance management, or process improvement ;
You are proficient in data analysis and visualization tools such as Power BI, Skywise, and Python;
You have in-depth knowledge of data warehousing, cloud analytics, and process automation;
You possess strong problem-solving skills and a demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams;
You have the ability to simplify complex data concepts for operational and executive leadership teams;
You have proven experience in defining performance measurement frameworks and creating complex analytical structures.

Business Travel May Be Required For This Position.

Travel requirements: < 5% (Occasional trips to the United States)

jobs.title: Director of Finance and Administration
jobs.description:
Lead financial and corporate stewardship for Curve Lake First Nation

Step into a senior leadership role offering a competitive $150,000 to $180,000 annual salary, negotiable based on qualifications, plus excellent benefits!

Build the systems, teams, and financial stability that will support the Nation for the next decade

About Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an Anishinaabe community with deep roots in this territory, grounded in relationships to land, water, and each other as Curve Lakers. Known historically as Mud Lake, Curve Lake continues as a living, resilient Nation of almost 3,000 members. As part of the Michi Saagiig Anishinaabeg and signatories to the Williams Treaties, the community carries forward its responsibilities, teachings, and governance systems. Curve Lake is a place of strong kinship, cultural continuity, and collective responsibility, where each member contributes to the wellbeing of the Nation. Our community is located just north of the City of Peterborough, Ontario.

Home to trailblazers like Elsie Knott, Canada's first Anishinaabe Kwe O'gimaa, and renowned artisans, our community blends rich history with vibrant culture. More than an employer, we're a community of choice. Join us in preserving traditions, fostering diversity, and contributing to a future where old ways merge seamlessly with progress. Shape the legacy of Curve Lake—a place where heritage meets opportunity.

To learn more about us, please visit: curvelakefirstnation.ca

About the Opportunity

Curve Lake First Nation has an exciting opportunity for a full-time, permanent Director of Finance and Administration
, based in Curve Lake, Ontario.
This role joins the organization during a period of organizational transition and growth.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will provide strategic leadership across the Nation’s corporate functions. These are financial governance, human resources, policy and planning, communications, and information technology. Finance sits at the heart of the role. You will be accountable for sound financial oversight, audit readiness, and strong relationships with funders, auditors, and the First Nations Financial Management Board.

Where We Are Now

The Nation is strengthening its administrative foundations; you will provide interim oversight and stabilization across Finance, HR, IT, and Policy and Planning while building out your team. You will also lead the selection and implementation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

A key priority is moving the Nation from year-by-year funding to Indigenous Services Canada’s 10-year grant. This means completing the Financial Management Board certification process and putting the controls and reporting in place to qualify. Predictable, long-term funding will give the Nation far greater confidence in its forecasting and planning.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, success will mean a fully staffed division with your managers in place, trusted relationships with Chief and Council, staff, and community, strengthened audit readiness and internal controls, and the ERP selection well underway.

By the end of year two, you will have led the Nation through FMB certification and embedded consistent financial, governance, and administrative practices. You will also have put systems in place that keep reporting and audits on schedule, giving the organization a solid foundation for the years ahead.

Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Leading multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and annual operating and capital budgets
Serving as executive lead for external audits, including selecting the appropriate audit firm and working closely with auditors throughout the process
Ensuring compliance with funding agreements, Indigenous Services Canada reporting requirements, and the Nation’s Financial Administration Law
Leading the Nation through the FMB certification and 10-year grant process
Structuring and staffing the finance function so reporting deadlines are consistently met, working with bookkeepers, analysts, and account managers
Providing executive oversight of HR, IT, policy and planning, and communications through four direct-report managers
Overseeing the selection and implementation of an ERP system, along with cybersecurity, data governance, and digital modernization
Providing financial analysis, risk advice, and recommendations to the Executive Director and Chief and Council

Due to the role's significance, refer to the Director of Finance and Administration document for a comprehensive overview beyond the listed duties.

More About You

To qualify, you will need a post-secondary degree or diploma in finance, accounting, or a related financial field
, along with at least 5 years of senior-level experience in financial administration or corporate services,
including experience working within a First Nation organization.

The following are required:
A valid Class G Driver’s Licence
Ability to undergo a criminal background check and vulnerable sector check
Willingness and ability to travel as required

The following skills and experience will be strong assets:
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation
Certified Aboriginal Financial Manager (CAFM) or Certified Aboriginal Professional Administrator (CAPA) designation
A master’s degree in public administration, finance, or a related field
Direct experience with the First Nations Financial Management Board, FMB certification, or the 10-year grant process
Strong working knowledge of audit processes, GAAP, and funder reporting requirements
Experience working with Indigenous Services Canada and other funding agencies
Experience overseeing multiple functional areas such as Finance, HR, IT, and Planning

As our ideal candidate, you are a disciplined, systems-minded leader who keeps deadlines met and audits clean, and who knows how to build a finance team organized around its reporting obligations. Your understanding of First Nation finances runs from day-to-day funding agreements through to the path toward long-term grant funding. Just as importantly, you lead with integrity, calm, and a people-centred approach, bringing an awareness of intergenerational trauma and its impact on workplaces and governance, along with a genuine respect for Curve Lake First Nation’s history, culture, and traditions.

Note: Preference will be given to applicants who have First Nation or Indigenous ancestry.

About the Benefits

In exchange for your hard work and dedication, you will receive a highly competitive salary of $150,000 to $180,000
negotiable dependent on experience, along with a great host of benefits, including:
Relocation assistance
Comprehensive Benefits Plan: extended health care, dental, vision, life and long-term disability, etc.
Competitive Pension Plan with up to 7.5% employer matching
40 paid hours for Special/Personal Leave Bereavement Leave
Paid time off for 17 designated days, including National Indigenous Day, Christmas Day, etc.
Generous vacation accrual
Paid sick days
Regular community events such as Pow Wows, Harvesters' Gatherings, Christmas Craft Shows, and more!

Take on a senior leadership role that builds lasting financial stability and strong systems for the Curve Lake First Nation community. Apply now!

jobs.title: Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement Strategy Speciality Portfolio
jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Responsibilities

The Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement Strategy Specialty Portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience) is accountable for the achievement of pricing, reimbursement and access for Lilly in-market brands and new products in the specialty portfolio.

This is a leadership rol where the incumbent leads, coaches and develops a team of head office-based Market Access Strategy Managers, and oversees activities related to the establishment and achievement of Market Access objectives for Launch brands, in-market brands and new product planning. The incumbent also owns the market access strategy for a key brand and undertakes work as an individual contributor to brand-specific activities.

The role reports to the Head of Pricing, Reimbursement and Market Access and partners closely with the Associate Director – Field Patient Access and Associate Director of Pricing to ensure continuous information-sharing and collaboration. As a member of the Market Access Leadership Team, the incumbent helps sets strategic direction for the department and ensures strong collaboration across teams and work streams.

Location:

This is a hybrid role – onsite presence at our Toronto office will be 10 days or more per month (or at least 50% of the time), determined in collaboration with your manager and based on business needs.

This role is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as participation in the Lilly Bonus Program and a car allowance.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Market Access Strategy & Leadership

Lead a team of head office-based Market Access Managers supporting the specialty portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience), including: goal-setting, performance management, capability building, project prioritization and resource allocation and budget ownership across brands and therapeutic areas;
Develop and coach team members to create a high performance team and encourage career development.
Provide strategic oversight for the following activities, undertaken by head office-based Market Access Managers across launch brands, in-market brands and new product planning:
Develop the Market Access Plan and pricing strategy for launch brands, in-market brands and new products, using collaborative, cross-functional mechanisms and collaboration with regional teams to ensure it is based on deep understanding of customer/stakeholder needs, as well as the needs and realities of the business
Ensure alignmenet from the affiliate leadership team on the core components of the Market Access Plan, namely: the Market Access objective, underlying assumptions and upsides/downsides; contingency plan; strategic intent and major tactics
Develop access solutions for out of pocket market including close collaboration with patient support program team.
Develop value dossiers for national and regional Health Technology Assessment (HTA) bodies and payers (public and private) including health economic arguments and models and robust budget impact analysis
Lead new product planning, including early Market Access assessments, pricing and access assumptions, and evidence needs ahead of launch, in partnership with international and cross-functional team
Lead in-market lifecycle planning for established brands, including new indications, listing renewals and response to changes in the policy environment

Collaborate with the associate director of pricing and forecasting to develop business cases for approval of list and net prices at the local level and above-country

Individual Key Brand Ownership

Own the end-to-end Market Access strategy for an assigned key brand, from the Market Access Plan through HTA submissions, provincial and private payer listings, out of pocket market solution and lifecycle management
Represent Market Access on the brand team and provide Market Access input into brand planning, forecasting and launch decisions
Act as the primary Market Access contact for the cross-functional brand team with Pricing, Medical, HEOR, RWE, Marketing and the field-based Patient Access team
Remain accountable for brand-level Market Access deliverables and timelines alongside people leadership responsibilities

Work closely with BBA’s multidisciplinary teams across Canada to ensure execution excellence and alignment with client objectives

Experience building and maturing a program delivery organization from a formative stage.

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. The Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement Strategy Specialty Portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience) is accountable for the achievement of pricing, reimbursement and access for Lilly in-market brands and new products in the specialty portfolio.

The incumbent also owns the market access strategy for a key brand and undertakes work as an individual contributor to brand-specific activities.

The role reports to the Head of Pricing, Reimbursement and Market Access and partners closely with the Associate Director – Field Patient Access and Associate Director of Pricing to ensure continuous information-sharing and collaboration. As a member of the Market Access Leadership Team, the incumbent helps sets strategic direction for the department and ensures strong collaboration across teams and work streams.

Location:

This is a hybrid role – onsite presence at our Toronto office will be 10 days or more per month (or at least 50% of the time), determined in collaboration with your manager and based on business needs.

This role is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as participation in the Lilly Bonus Program and a car allowance.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Lead a team of head office-based Market Access Managers supporting the specialty portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience), including: goal-setting, performance management, capability building, project prioritization and resource allocation and budget ownership across brands and therapeutic areas;
Develop and coach team members to create a high performance team and encourage career development.

Lead in-market lifecycle planning for established brands, including new indications, listing renewals and response to changes in the policy environment

Collaborate with the associate director of pricing and forecasting to develop business cases for approval of list and net prices at the local level and above-country

Individual Key Brand Ownership

Own the end-to-end Market Access strategy for an assigned key brand, from the Market Access Plan through HTA submissions, provincial and private payer listings, out of pocket market solution and lifecycle management
Represent Market Access on the brand team and provide Market Access input into brand planning, forecasting and launch decisions
Act as the primary Market Access contact for the cross-functional brand team with Pricing, Medical, HEOR, RWE, Marketing and the field-based Patient Access team
Remain accountable for brand-level Market Access deliverables and timelines alongside people leadership responsibilities

Bachelor’s degree or higher required, ideally in a scientific field
